target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

## What Problem This Solves

Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading, caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, block the loop for 14-22 seconds and drop messages (issue #87509 reports 14-22s bootstrap-context stalls that block channel I/O, WebSocket keepalive, and timers).

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

## Why This Change Was Made

Bootstrap extra-file loading runs during embedded-run bootstrap-context, on the hot path that prepares every agent turn. On `main` the exported loader reaches Node `fs.glob` and synchronous fd reads, which monopolize the event loop over a large workspace; this change routes the same exported loader through an async yielding walker and async fd reads, and yields between bootstrap hook handlers, so channel I/O stays responsive during bootstrap. The public plugin SDK surface is deliberately unchanged.

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

## User Impact

Agents whose workspaces contain large trees or broad `bootstrap-extra-files` globs no longer stall the event loop for seconds during bootstrap-context, so WebSocket keepalives, typing indicators, HTTP requests, and timers keep firing while an agent turn is being prepared — messages are no longer dropped. The set of bootstrap files loaded is unchanged (identical glob match set), so no agent sees different context. Root bootstrap file loading goes serial-sync → parallel-async, glob walks go blocking → yielding, and hook chains go uninterrupted → yielded.

## Evidence

This is a **current-`main` vs current-PR-head** real-behavior benchmark against the real exported loader, covering elapsed time, event-loop responsiveness, glob-match parity, and RSS.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces (issue #87509). This change replaces the native `fs.glob` walk with an async walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries so the event loop stays responsive, while returning the identical configured `bootstrap-extra-files` match set.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. `main` = `9b823c610816` (native `fs.glob`, synchronous fd reads); head = `3dfd7f1d4952` (async yielding walker, async fd reads). The identical benchmark script runs inside each checkout (relative import binds to that checkout's implementation); both consume the same pre-built read-only workspace.
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of **395,807 filesystem entries** (391,124 files, 4,683 dirs — wide flat dirs + a deep 40-level tree + `node_modules` + `.git` + `.hidden` noise), with `AGENTS.md` planted at several depths (root, deep-past-old-cutoff, `.hidden/`, `node_modules/`). Configured pattern `**/AGENTS.md`. During the load a 5ms repeating timer counts liveness ticks, `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay({resolution:5})` records event-loop delay, and `process.memoryUsage().rss` is captured before/after with `global.gc()`. 3 fresh processes per side after a discarded warmup; values below are medians.
- **Failing proof before fix** (current `main` `9b823c610816`, native `fs.glob`):
  ```
  elapsed: 834.5ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 55.5ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 8.50ms   p99: 54.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 95 / 166 expected (57.2% kept)
  rssDelta: 358.3 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: fs.glob finishes the walk fast but monopolizes the loop —
          multi-tens-of-ms stalls, ~43% of 5ms liveness ticks dropped, 358 MB RSS spike
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch** (identical script both sides; full reproduce recipe below):
  ```
  # build the shared 395,807-entry workspace once, then run each side from its own checkout
  node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws"
  ```
- **Evidence after fix** (current PR head `3dfd7f1d4952`, async yielding walker):
  ```
  elapsed: 1244.8ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 10.7ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 5.09ms   p99: 6.6ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 245 / 248 expected (98.8% kept)
  rssDelta: 57.0 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: yielding walker keeps the loop responsive — max delay near the 5ms floor,
          98.8% of liveness ticks fired, RSS footprint ~6x smaller
  ```
- **Glob result parity (main vs head)**: sha256 of the sorted relative match set is **identical** on both sides — `b90d55afa71f2aa871ea40de7d91715377c93b76d26e7f43d817019b6b72a97e`. Matched set both sides: `AGENTS.md`, the deep 40-level `deep/.../AGENTS.md`, and `node_modules/pkg000/AGENTS.md`; `.git` and `.hidden/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded by both. The custom walker changes event-loop behavior and memory, not the returned file set.

  | metric (median of 3, 395,807 entries, Node v24.10.0) | main `9b823c610816` | head `3dfd7f1d4952` |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | elapsed (ms) | 834.5 | 1244.8 |
  | max event-loop delay (ms) | 55.5 | 10.7 |
  | mean event-loop delay (ms) | 8.50 | 5.09 |
  | liveness ticks kept | 57.2% | 98.8% |
  | RSS delta (MB) | 358.3 | 57.0 |
  | `**/AGENTS.md` matches returned | 3 | 3 (identical set) |

- **Observed result after fix**: the fix trades a modest wall-clock increase (834ms → 1245ms) for the property the issue actually needs — the event loop stops stalling. Max event-loop delay drops from 55.5ms to 10.7ms (near the 5ms probe floor), liveness-tick retention rises from 57.2% to 98.8%, and peak RSS is ~6x smaller (358MB → 57MB) because the walker no longer buffers the whole `fs.glob` result eagerly. The returned match set is byte-identical (same sha256), so existing `bootstrap-extra-files` configs load the same files. At the field-report scale (much larger real workspaces), `main`'s blocking walk is what produces the 14-22s embedded_run stalls; this benchmark demonstrates the direction and mechanism (blocking `fs.glob` vs cooperative yielding) at 395,807 entries on a single dev box.
- **Reproduce**:
  ```bash
  BENCH=/tmp/bench-89040
  PR=<pr-head-checkout>
  git -C "$PR" worktree add --detach "$BENCH/main-wt" 9b823c610816   # current upstream/main
  ln -s "$PR/node_modules" "$BENCH/main-wt/node_modules"             # read-only bench, first-party deps
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$PR/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$BENCH/main-wt/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  # build the shared workspace once (reused by both sides, walk mutates nothing)
  (cd "$PR" && node --import tsx/esm "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" build "$BENCH/ws" 400000)
  # 3 fresh processes per side, run from inside each checkout so the relative import binds
  (cd "$PR"            && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  (cd "$BENCH/main-wt" && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  ```
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real exported glob-resolution path (`loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`) and event-loop instrumentation directly rather than through a connected channel. The main-side `node_modules` is symlinked from the head checkout, which is valid because `workspace.ts`'s transitive imports are first-party and the run is read-only. Focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(google): anchor model-ID regexes to prevent false-positive substring matches
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Model-ID matching in `google-shared.ts` uses substring patterns that match false positives on hypenated lookalikes (e.g. `gemini-2.5-flash` matches `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`).

**Solution**: Replace loose `\b` word-boundary suffixes with `(?![a-z0-9-])` negative lookahead — an explicit model-ID contract that only allows end-of-string or non-identifier continuation (e.g. `@`, spaces). All 6 model-ID regexes and `String.includes()` calls are now properly anchored.

## Changes

| Regex | Before | After |
|------|------|------|
| isGemma4Model | `/gemma-?4/` | `/(?:^|\/)gemma-?4(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| isGemini3ProModel | `/gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-pro/` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-pro(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| isGemini3FlashModel | `/gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-flash/` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-flash(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| 2.5-pro budget | `.includes("2.5-pro")` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-pro(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| 2.5-flash-lite budget | `.includes("2.5-flash-lite")` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-flash-lite(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| 2.5-flash budget | `.includes("2.5-flash")` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-flash(?![a-z0-9-])/` |

The `(?![a-z0-9-])` negative lookahead prevents matching when followed by model-name continuation characters:
- `gemini-2.5-flash` does NOT match `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` (hyphen suffix rejected)
- `gemini-2.5-flash` DOES match `gemini-2.5-flash@preview` (allowed suffix)

target.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — UI dashboard and CLI command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
There is no UI or CLI surface for observing AI safety events. Operators cannot see prompt injection signals, tool policy decisions, or eval scores without digging into raw OTEL exports.

## Evidence
- `openclaw safety events` CLI command added (run `openclaw safety events --help` to see options: `--type`, `--session`, `--since`, `--limit`, `--severity`, `--json`)
- `ui/src/pages/safety/` — new Lit-based safety page at `/safety` with KPI strip and event table
- `/safety` route added to sidebar nav
- `src/infra/safety-event-store.ts` — in-memory ring buffer (10k cap) with cursor-paginated query API
- `src/gateway/server-methods/safety.ts` — `safety.events.list` and `safety.events.summary` RPC handlers
- MVP uses in-memory store; SQLite persistence flagged as next step in PR description
- Depends on: #107176, #107184

## Evidence — Clawsweeper re-review fixes (2026-07-14)

**Rebase:** rebased onto the updated #107184 (which itself carries the #107176 security fix), picking up the untrusted-path exclusion of AI safety events and the OTEL emitter-provenance attributes. Also fixed a typecheck failure surfaced by the rebase: `getSafetyEventStore()` passed a string key to `resolveGlobalSingleton`, which requires a `Symbol.for(...)` key (matches all other call sites). `pnpm tsgo` is clean on this branch.

**4-PR series design note:** the security boundary is deliberate across the stack — #107176 defines the contracts and excludes AI safety events from the untrusted emit surface (type- and runtime-gated); #107184 wires exporters and preserves emitter provenance; #107187 adds the only plugin-facing emission surface, gated by manifest `safetyEventTypes`; this PR adds the UI/CLI observability surfaces. Untrusted path gated, trusted path only.

**OTEL note:** full end-to-end OTEL integration proof requires a running collector, which is not available in CI; exporter behavior is covered by unit tests in #107184.

### Live simulation output
<details>
<summary>Terminal output — emitting all 6 event types through trusted path (re-run 2026-07-14 after rebase onto upstream/main)</summary>

Run: `npx tsx scripts/simulate-ai-safety-events.ts` on `feat/ai-safety-exporters` (script committed in that branch). Stages: trusted emit → dispatcher fan-out → spoof-resistance gate (untrusted emissions dropped) → OTEL exporter recorders.

```

=== OpenClaw AI Safety Event Taxonomy — Simulation Run ===
Schema version: 1
Session: sim-session-abc12345

--- Stage 1: emit through trusted core path ---
  emit → ai_safety.prompt_injection.signal ... ok
  emit → ai_safety.tool_policy.decision ... ok
  emit → ai_safety.external_content.consumed ... ok
  emit → ai_safety.user_feedback.received ... ok
  emit → ai_safety.memory_context.selected ... ok
  emit → ai_safety.eval.result ... ok

--- Stage 2: dispatcher fan-out (trusted metadata attached) ---
  dispatch → ai_safety.prompt_injection.signal (seq=1, trusted=true)
  dispatch → ai_safety.tool_policy.decision (seq=2, trusted=true)
  dispatch → ai_safety.external_content.consumed (seq=3, trusted=true)
  dispatch → ai_safety.user_feedback.received (seq=4, trusted=true)
  dispatch → ai_safety.memory_context.selected (seq=5, trusted=true)
  dispatch → ai_safety.eval.result (seq=6, trusted=true)

--- Stage 3: spoof-resistance gate (untrusted plugin path) ---
  untrusted emit → ai_safety.prompt_injection.signal ... submitted
  untrusted emit → ai_safety.tool_policy.decision ... submitted
  untrusted emit → ai_safety.external_content.consumed ... submitted
  untrusted emit → ai_safety.user_feedback.received ... submitted
  untrusted emit → ai_safety.memory_context.selected ... submitted
  untrusted emit → ai_safety.eval.result ... submitted
  result: 0/6 untrusted ai_safety.* events reached the dispatcher (expected 0 — dropped by anti-spoofing gate)

--- Stage 4: OTEL exporter recorders (counter + low-cardinality attrs) ---
  otel counter openclaw.ai_safety.prompt_injection.signal += 1
      openclaw.ai_safety.emitter_trusted = "true"
      openclaw.ai_safety.severity = "warn"
      openclaw.ai_safety.category = "indirect"
      openclaw.ai_safety.action_taken = "flagged"
      openclaw.ai_safety.source_type = "tool_output"
      openclaw.ai_safety.channel = "whatsapp"
  otel counter openclaw.ai_safety.tool_policy.decision += 1
      openclaw.ai_safety.emitter_trusted = "true"
      openclaw.ai_safety.tool_name = "bash"
      openclaw.ai_safety.decision = "approval_required"
      openclaw.ai_safety.policy_source = "static_config"
      openclaw.ai_safety.severity = "warn"
```

Plugins have no typed, policy-enforced API for emitting AI safety events. Without it, third-party detectors (prompt injection scanners, source-trust validators) cannot contribute to the taxonomy in a safe, auditable way.

## Evidence

The AI safety event types defined in #107176 need to be wired to the existing OTEL and Prometheus exporters so operators can observe them in their telemetry stacks. Without exporter mappings, the events are emitted but invisible.

## Evidence

target.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — core event contracts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
OpenClaw has operational diagnostics, OTEL exporters, and prompt-injection hardening, but no first-class AI safety/quality event taxonomy. Without a shared schema, safety signals (prompt injection attempts, tool policy decisions, external content ingestion, eval scores) are invisible to operators and cannot be correlated across sessions or exported consistently.

## Evidence
- `src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts` — `DiagnosticSecurityEvent.category` enum confirms no `ai_safety` category exists in main
- Clawsweeper review of issue #82548 (June 29) confirmed current main does not have the requested taxonomy
- New types: `ai_safety.prompt_injection.signal`, `ai_safety.tool_policy.decision`, `ai_safety.external_content.consumed`, `ai_safety.user_feedback.received`, `ai_safety.memory_context.selected`, `ai_safety.eval.result`
- 8 unit tests added in `src/infra/diagnostic-events.test.ts` covering each new event type and schema version constant
- Depends on: nothing (this is the unblocking schema PR)
- Unblocks: #107184 (exporters), #107187 (plugin API), #107192 (UI/CLI)

## Evidence — Clawsweeper re-review fixes (2026-07-14)

**Security fix:** `DiagnosticAISafetyEventPayload` is now excluded from `DiagnosticEventInput` (the untrusted `emitDiagnosticEvent()` surface). AI safety events are emittable only via the trusted core path (`emitTrustedDiagnosticEvent`, new `TrustedDiagnosticEventInput` type) or the policy-gated `emitPluginSafetyEvent` from #107187. A runtime gate mirroring the existing `security.event` gate additionally drops any `ai_safety.*` event emitted untrusted, so plugins cannot spoof safety findings even with an unsafe cast. Contract tests moved to `src/infra/diagnostic-ai-safety-events.test.ts` and now cover the untrusted-drop behavior:

```

✓ diagnostic AI safety events > all six AI safety event types carry standard seq/ts enrichment

```

**4-PR series design note:** the security boundary is deliberate across the stack — this PR defines the contracts and locks the untrusted path; #107184 wires exporters and preserves emitter provenance; #107187 adds the only plugin-facing emission surface, gated by manifest `safetyEventTypes`; #107192 adds observability surfaces. Untrusted path gated, trusted path only.

**OTEL note:** full end-to-end OTEL integration proof requires a running collector, which is not available in CI; exporter behavior is covered by unit tests in #107184.

target.title: fix(discord): keep voice participant labels UTF-16 safe [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord voice participant labels (nick / global name / username) could end up with a dangling UTF-16 surrogate half when the label is longer than 100 code units and an emoji lands on the truncation boundary.

`normalizeLabel` in `extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.ts` (introduced in #107004) truncated with a plain `normalized.slice(0, 100)`. Discord nicks and global names regularly contain emoji. When an emoji's surrogate pair straddles the 100-code-unit boundary, `slice(0, 100)` keeps the high surrogate and drops the low one, leaving a dangling `\uD83D`-style half that renders as `�` and can corrupt downstream JSON serialization / logs that consume the formatted participant line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix swaps the bare `slice(0, 100)` for the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (from `@openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`), which is already used across the Discord extension (`error-body.ts`, `monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`, `monitor/message-handler.context.ts`, etc.) and across ~300 call sites repo-wide for exactly this class of truncation. Same pattern as #102246 (mushuiyu886, merged) and dozens of zhangguiping-xydt / mushuiyu886 UTF-16 safe truncation PRs.

The change is one import + one call-site replacement in `participant-context.ts`; no behavior change for labels that fit or that don't land an emoji on the boundary.

## User Impact

Voice participant lines (`- user_id=... display_name=...`) rendered to the agent / logs no longer carry a `�` or a dangling surrogate when a long Discord nick/global name is truncated mid-emoji. Labels <= 100 code units are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real behavior captured by driving the real exported `formatDiscordVoiceParticipantStateLine` with a participant whose nick is `"m".repeat(99) + "😀"` (101 UTF-16 code units - the emoji's surrogate pair straddles the 100 boundary).

**Before fix (current `main`)** - `slice(0, 100)` splits the `😀` surrogate pair, leaving a dangling high surrogate:

```
nick_length: 101
label_length: 100
has_dangling_surrogate: true
label_preview: "mmmm\ud83d"
```

**After fix** - `truncateUtf16Safe` backs the boundary off the surrogate pair:

```
nick_length: 101
label_length: 99
has_dangling_surrogate: false
label_preview: "mmmmm"
```

Regression test in `extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.test.ts` (`keeps participant labels UTF-16 safe when an emoji lands on the truncate boundary`): failing-first, asserts the parsed `display_name` label has no dangling surrogate and stays within 100 code units.

Local verification:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.test.ts` - 2/2 pass (failing-first on `main`).
- `oxlint` + `oxfmt --check` on changed files - pass.

Not tested: live Discord voice state events (the proof drives the real `formatDiscordVoiceParticipantStateLine` formatter directly with a participant state shaped like a real `APIVoiceState.member.nick`).

target.title: fix(sessions-send): normalize sourceSessionKey to dmScope-resolved canonical key
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `session.dmScope` is `"main"` (default), inter-agent messages sent via `sessions_send` embed the calling session persisted storage key as `sourceSessionKey` — even when that key was created under a previous `per-account-channel-peer` routing regime. The receiving agent replies to the stale key, creating a ghost session that the sender never monitors, causing permanent one-way communication failure between agents.

**Split path:**
1. **Inbound user DMs** → resolved via `buildAgentPeerSessionKey()` with `dmScope="main"` → lands in `agent:{id}:main` ✓
2. **Inter-session replies** → routed to `sourceSessionKey` from provenance → lands in `agent:{id}:{channel}:{account}:direct:{peer}` (stale format) ✗

Two different session keys → two different sessions → the agent in session A never sees replies delivered to session B.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `sessions_send` tool passed `opts.agentSessionKey` verbatim into `inputProvenance.sourceSessionKey`. This is the session persisted key from storage, not a dmScope-resolved key. The fix normalizes the requester key through `buildAgentMainSessionKey()` when `dmScope` is `"main"`, so all downstream provenance, watch registration, same-session detection, and A2A ping-pong routing use the same canonical key that the agent actually monitors.

## User Impact

Multi-agent setups using `dmScope="main"` (the default) with sessions that predate a routing regime change will now correctly route inter-agent replies back to the sender monitored session. No config changes required. Operators with `dmScope` set to `per-peer`, `per-channel-peer`, or `per-account-channel-peer` are unaffected — the normalization only activates when `dmScope` is `"main"`.

## Evidence

- `sessions-send-helpers.test.ts`: **10/10 passed**
- `sessions-send-tool.a2a.test.ts`: **25/25 passed**
- oxfmt and git diff --check clean

Fixes #107399

target.title: fix(cli): restore terminal state before exit in logs and hooks commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`process.exit(1)` in `logs-cli.ts:685` and `hooks-cli.ts:153` bypasses the CLI's standard exit path (`runtime.exit()`), which calls `restoreTerminalState()` before terminating. This means the terminal state (raw mode, cursor visibility, ANSI reset sequences, active progress line) is not cleaned up when these commands exit on error.

Additionally, the hooks-cli replacement (`defaultRuntime.exit(1)`) breaks the `never` type contract because `defaultRuntime.exit()` returns `void`, not `never`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every other CLI command uses `runtime.exit()` → `restoreTerminalState()` → `process.exit()` as defined in `src/runtime.ts:89-96`. These two call sites were the only exceptions.

This revision routes both error paths through the canonical `defaultRuntime.exit(1)`:
- **hooks-cli.ts**: Added `throw new Error("unreachable")` after `defaultRuntime.exit(1)` — matches the same pattern in `src/runtime.ts:94` that preserves the `never` return type contract and satisfies tests when `process.exit` is mocked
- **logs-cli.ts**: Replaced manual `restoreTerminalState()` + `process.exit(1)` with `defaultRuntime.exit(1)`, eliminating the duplicated cleanup and the now-unused `restoreTerminalState` import

## User Impact

Very low in practice — `logs follow` does not set raw mode itself, and `restoreTerminalState()` operations all have TTY guards. But it is a defensive fix to ensure terminal state is always restored on exit, consistent with the rest of the CLI contract.

## Evidence

- **Contract**: `src/runtime.ts:89-96` — `defaultRuntime.exit()` calls `restoreTerminalState("runtime exit", ...)` before `process.exit()`
- **Consistency**: All other CLI commands (config, plugins-search, devices, gateway run-loop) use `runtime.exit()`
- **Commit history**: `git blame` confirms the raw `process.exit(1)` was added in the initial monorepo import commit with no subsequent discussion or adjustment

### Tests
- `pnpm test src/cli/hooks-cli.test.ts` — 5/5 passed
- `pnpm test src/cli/logs-cli.test.ts` — 37/37 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed (prod type check)
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed (test type check)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint` — clean
- `pnpm format:check` — passed

### Real Behavior Proof

**Setup**: Built CLI from branch (`1d76252`), ran inside a PTY (`script -q -c "..." /dev/null`) so `process.stdin.isTTY=true` and `process.stdout.isTTY=true`, ensuring all `restoreTerminalState()` code paths execute.

`restoreTerminalState()` in `packages/terminal-core/src/restore.ts` does four things on TTY:
1. `clearActiveProgressLine()` — clears any active progress line
2. `stdin.setRawMode(false)` — exits raw mode if previously set
3. `process.stdout.write(RESET_SEQUENCE)` — sends the ANSI escape sequence:
   `\x1b[0m\x1b[?25h\x1b[?1000l\x1b[?1002l\x1b[?1003l\x1b[?1006l\x1b[?2004l\x1b[<u\x1b[>4;0m`
   (reset attributes, show cursor, disable mouse tracking ×4, disable bracketed paste, reset modifyCursorKeys, reset modifyOtherKeys)

**Proof 1 — logs --follow fatal error path** (full terminal output):
```
$ openclaw logs --follow --url ws://127.0.0.1:18789
[agent-scope] Multiple agents marked default=true; using the first entry as default.

◇  Config warnings ─────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - plugins.entries.voice-call: plugin disabled ...         │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
Gateway not reachable. Is it running and accessible?
Gateway target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789
Source: cli --url
Config: /home/0668000452/.openclaw/openclaw.json
Hint: run `openclaw doctor`.
←─ RESET_SEQUENCE emitted here (see hex evidence below)
>>> exit code: 1
```

**Proof 2 — hooks enable error path** (full terminal output):
```
$ openclaw hooks enable nonexistent-hook
[agent-scope] Multiple agents marked default=true; using the first entry as default.

◇  Config warnings ─────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - plugins.entries.voice-call: plugin disabled ...         │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
Error: Hook "nonexistent-hook" not found
←─ RESET_SEQUENCE emitted here (see hex evidence below)
>>> exit code: 1
```

**ANSI reset sequence hex evidence** (extracted from both command outputs):

Both error paths emit the identical ANSI reset sequence after the error message:
```
ESC[0m        ← reset all SGR attributes (colors, bold, etc.)
ESC[?25h      ← show cursor (DECTCEM)
ESC[?1000l    ← disable basic mouse tracking
ESC[?1002l    ← disable button-event mouse tracking
ESC[?1003l    ← disable any-event mouse tracking
ESC[?1006l    ← disable SGR mouse mode
ESC[?2004l    ← disable bracketed paste mode
ESC[<u        ← reset modifyCursorKeys
ESC[>4;0m     ← reset modifyOtherKeys
```

This sequence matches the `RESET_SEQUENCE` constant in `packages/terminal-core/src/restore.ts` exactly, proving `restoreTerminalState()` was called.

**Exit code verification**: Both commands exit with code `1` (from `defaultRuntime.exit(1)` → `process.exit(1)`), not timeout (124).

**Terminal function verification**: After exit, `tput cols` (80 columns), `tput cnorm` (show cursor), and `tput setaf` (color output) all work correctly, confirming terminal state is restored.

### What Was Not Tested

- `hooks relay` command error path (requires a running agent session)
- `hooks install` / `hooks update` error paths (require plugin registry)
- TTY with raw mode previously set by Node.js `setRawMode(true)` — shell `stty raw` is not tracked by libuv, so `setRawMode(false)` is a no-op in this test. However, all operations in `restoreTerminalState()` have TTY guards and try/catch, and `process.stdout.write(RESET_SEQUENCE)` is idempotent. The ANSI reset sequence is emitted regardless, which is the primary defense against terminal state corruption.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/cli/hooks-cli.ts` | Add `throw new Error("unreachable")` after `defaultRuntime.exit(1)` to preserve `never` type contract |
| `src/cli/logs-cli.ts` | Replace manual `restoreTerminalState` + `process.exit(1)` with canonical `defaultRuntime.exit(1)` |
| `src/cli/logs-cli.test.ts` | Add `vi.mock("../runtime.js")` to prevent runtime's unreachable throw from escaping when tests mock `process.exit` |

target.title: fix(cli): wrap readFileSync ENOENT with user-friendly error messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three CLI code paths in `src/cli/` leak raw Node.js `ENOENT` errors with full absolute filesystem paths when the user supplies a nonexistent file path. This is noisy and exposes internal implementation details.

**Before (all three paths):**
```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/home/user/.openclaw/some/internal/path'
```

**After:**
```
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: Secrets plan file not found: /tmp/missing-plan.json
Error: --file not found: /bad/patch.json5
```

The user-supplied path is retained in the message (it is input the user provided, so it helps them spot typos), but the raw Node.js error code and any derived internal paths are removed. The original error is preserved via `{ cause: err }` so upstream error reporters can still access the underlying `ENOENT` if needed.

Fixes #N/A (no linked issue)

## Why This Change Was Made

Affected surfaces:

| File | User action | Error |
|------|-------------|-------|
| `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:139` | `openclaw config set --batch-file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:55` | `openclaw secrets apply <bad-plan-file>` | `ENOENT` raw error |
| `src/cli/config-cli.ts:1497` | `openclaw config patch --file <bad-path>` | `ENOENT` raw error |

Each fix wraps `readFileSync` in a try-catch that checks `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT"` and throws a descriptive `Error` with the user-facing flag name, the original path, and the original error as `cause`. Non-ENOENT errors are re-thrown unchanged. The `cause` property satisfies the `preserve-caught-error` lint rule and allows upstream callers to inspect the underlying filesystem error.

## User Impact

- Users who mistype a `--batch-file`, `--file`, or secrets plan path see a clean, actionable error message instead of a raw Node.js stack trace.
- No change to the success path or any other error path. Error class remains `Error` (not a new subclass), so existing `catch` / `instanceof` logic is unaffected.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — 156/156 passing (includes 3 ENOENT regression tests covering all 3 command paths)
- `oxlint --quiet` on all 6 touched files — clean
- `oxfmt --check` on all 6 touched files — clean

### Real CLI proof (after `pnpm build`)

**Command 1: `config set --batch-file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config set --batch-file /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
Error: --batch-file not found: /nonexistent/path/batch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 2: `config patch --file`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw config patch --file /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
Error: --file not found: /nonexistent/path/patch.json5
EXIT: 1
```

**Command 3: `secrets apply --from`**
```
$ pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from /nonexistent/path/plan.json
Secrets apply failed: Secrets plan file not found: /nonexistent/path/plan.json ...
EXIT: 1
```

Behavior addressed: All three CLI commands now produce user-friendly ENOENT errors.
Real environment tested: Linux dev workstation, Node 22, `pnpm build` then `pnpm openclaw ...`.
What was not tested: Windows/macOS file permission errors (non-ENOENT); those are re-thrown unchanged.

target.title: fix(ai): record token usage on Responses early-abort (#100954)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Azure/OpenAI Responses streams that end early with `response.incomplete` (e.g. `max_output_tokens` reached, content filter) never send `response.completed`. Both Responses stream processors on `main` assign `output.usage` **only** inside the `response.completed` branch, so these early-terminated streams leave usage — and its cost — at zero, dropping the reported token counts (including partial cache-hit tokens) and their cost from telemetry and session accounting. This is the drift described in #100954.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `response.incomplete` event carries a full `Response` object with the same `usage` shape (`input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `total_tokens` + `input_tokens_details`) as `response.completed`. The fix records that usage — **and computes its cost** — when the stream terminates early. Both Responses processors had the identical completed-only defect, so both are fixed:
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts`
- `src/agents/openai-responses-transport.ts`

Both `response.completed` and the new `response.incomplete` branch route through one terminal usage+cost path (map usage → `calculateCost` → service-tier pricing). Cost must run for the incomplete path too because session accounting sums `usage.cost.total` (`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`); recording tokens without cost would still under-report. Stop-reason mapping and completed-only backfill stay specific to `response.completed`. The abort lifecycle already forwards a populated `output.usage` into the emitted error event, so no changes to the abort path or the generic `normalizeUsage` were needed.

## Single Billing Source of Truth

Per review feedback ([P1] "use one canonical terminal-usage helper"), the terminal usage/cost invariant now lives in **one** shared mapper — `mapResponsesTerminalUsage` in `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-terminal-usage.ts`, re-exported via `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai`. It performs the priced bucket split, `calculateCost`, and service-tier pricing. Both processors call it:

- The package processor's `recordResponsesTerminalUsage` writes the priced usage onto the package `AssistantMessage`.
- The agent transport uses a thin adapter that adds only the agent-local `reasoningTokens` field, which the normalized `Usage` type (`packages/llm-core/src/types.ts`) does not model — it is tracked separately by the agent usage accumulator and diagnostics. The shared mapper returns a `Usage`; the agent layers reasoning on top.

No billing logic is duplicated across the two processors, and the previous agent-side `as never` casts are gone.

## User Impact

Token usage **and cost** telemetry stay accurate when a Responses stream is cut short, instead of silently reporting zero. No change to normal (`response.completed`) streams or to provider defaults.

## Evidence

Regression tests drive a real `response.incomplete` event (carrying nonzero tokens, including cache reads/writes) through the actual stream processors with **no** `response.completed`, then assert both the token buckets and a nonzero computed cost:

- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` → **52 passed** (early-abort test asserts `usage.cost.total > 0` and exact per-bucket cost)
- `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` → **331 passed** (same regression added for the sibling processor)

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp

      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:


## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Summary

- Problem: new Control UI dashboard sessions without a label/displayName fall back to raw session keys, making multiple new chats hard to distinguish.
- Solution: add a Control UI fallback that renders unnamed dashboard sessions as their local creation time.
- What changed: gateway session rows now expose `sessionStartedAt`; Control UI uses it for dashboard-session display fallback, with `updatedAt` as a legacy fallback.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no persisted labels are written, no rename UI was added, and explicit labels/display names still win.

AI-assisted: yes. I used a local coding agent and ran the verification below myself.

## Motivation

- Closes #86040.

## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.

## Validation

- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRTUXB | tr '\n' ' ')`
- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run ui/src/components/form-controls.browser.test.ts ui/src/pages/config/quick.test.ts ui/src/pages/config/view.browser.test.ts ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts`

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
Related: #104485

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Crabbox agent commands were forced onto Blacksmith Testbox even when an operator had selected another eligible provider through `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`. That made machine-local provider preferences ineffective and could also cause local-container execution to be described as remote/Testbox proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns the root policy and both Crabbox/testing skills on one provider-selection contract:

1. Source trust, platform, and proof requirements determine eligible providers.
2. An explicit eligible provider requested by the user wins.
3. Ordinary eligible wrapper calls omit `--provider`, allowing `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` to override the repository default.
4. With no user or environment preference, Blacksmith Testbox remains the repository fallback.

The same contract is applied to the root policy plus the Crabbox, testing, and PR-maintainer skills, so PR workflows cannot reintroduce mandatory Testbox routing. This restores the original goal of #104485 without weakening the sanitized-AWS/secretless-CI requirements for untrusted source. It is the maintained replacement because the original PR branch could not be updated. Original contributor: @hxy91819.

## User Impact

Operators can set a machine-local preference such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container` without changing the shared skill. AWS or another eligible provider can be selected the same way. Task-specific user requests still take priority, while unsafe or platform-incompatible choices remain blocked.

## Evidence

- Current head: `32452922d779597437621cdf63fb02d740b49837`.
- Dependency contract checked in Crabbox source: config files load before environment overrides, `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` overrides the configured provider, and an explicit CLI `--provider` remains the final override.
- Claude via acpx independently routed the policy cases correctly: env `local-container` -> local Docker proof with no explicit provider; unset env -> Blacksmith fallback; untrusted credential-hydrated Testbox request -> sanitized AWS or secretless CI.
- A second Claude/acpx audit read all four active policy surfaces and found no remaining mandatory-Testbox or eager-prewarm contradiction. The mandatory hosted Testbox check in `scripts/pr prepare-run` is a merge-gate verification contract, not provider selection.
- Claude via acpx ran a real inherited-provider command with no explicit `--provider`: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_b5d22ebde587 --no-sync --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts`.
- Wrapper output: `provider=local-container`, lease `cbx_b5d22ebde587`, local Docker proof, 195/195 tests passed, exit 0. Cleanup verified: container removed and lease status returned not found.
- `oxfmt --check AGENTS.md .agents/skills/crabbox/SKILL.md .agents/skills/openclaw-testing/SKILL.md`
- `git diff --check`
- Fresh autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Exact-head GitHub checks are pending.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text

codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Current review state

AI-assisted: yes.

Next action: maintainer review.

target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: new Control UI dashboard sessions without a label/displayName fall back to raw session keys, making multiple new chats hard to distinguish.
- Solution: add a Control UI fallback that renders unnamed dashboard sessions as their local creation time.
- What changed: gateway session rows now expose `sessionStartedAt`; Control UI uses it for dashboard-session display fallback, with `updatedAt` as a legacy fallback.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no persisted labels are written, no rename UI was added, and explicit labels/display names still win.

AI-assisted: yes. I used a local coding agent and ran the verification below myself.

## Motivation

- Closes #86040.
- This is a low-friction UX improvement for users who create several dashboard chats with `/NEW` and need to pick the right session at a glance.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #86040
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: unnamed Control UI dashboard sessions now display a local timestamp fallback instead of the raw `agent:<id>:dashboard:<uuid>` key, while named sessions still display their explicit label.
- Real environment tested: macOS 26.5 (25F71), local OpenClaw checkout at this PR branch, Node v23.11.0, pnpm 11.2.2.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - `pnpm --dir ui exec tsx -e "import { resolveSessionDisplayName } from './src/ui/session-display.ts'; const key = 'agent:ops:dashboard:chat-proof'; const now = new Date(2026, 4, 24, 22, 0); const sameDay = resolveSessionDisplayName(key, { key, kind: 'direct', updatedAt: 200, sessionStartedAt: new Date(2026, 4, 24, 14, 12).getTime() }, { now }); const priorDay = resolveSessionDisplayName('agent:ops:dashboard:chat-proof-2', { key: 'agent:ops:dashboard:chat-proof-2', kind: 'direct', updatedAt: 200, sessionStartedAt: new Date(2026, 4, 23, 9, 5).getTime() }, { now }); const named = resolveSessionDisplayName(key, { key, kind: 'direct', updatedAt: 200, label: 'Bug triage', sessionStartedAt: new Date(2026, 4, 24, 14, 12).getTime() }, { now }); console.log(JSON.stringify({ sameDay, priorDay, named }, null, 2));"`
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```json
{
  "sameDay": "14:12",
  "priorDay": "05-23 09:05",
  "named": "Bug triage"
}
```

- Observed result after fix: same-day unnamed dashboard sessions render `HH:mm`, prior-day unnamed dashboard sessions render `MM-DD HH:mm`, and explicit labels remain unchanged.
- What was not tested: I did not run a full local gateway plus browser session with a live `/NEW` interaction. The focused runtime proof above imports the actual Control UI helper, and the browser/unit tests below cover the UI helper/controller surfaces.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): the new RED test initially failed with `expected 'agent:ops:dashboard:chat-1' to be '14:12'` before the implementation.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: N/A, this is a feature request.
- Missing detection / guardrail: unnamed dashboard-session display fallback was not covered.
- Contributing context (if known): dashboard session rows already had durable `sessionStartedAt`, but the projected gateway row did not expose it to the UI.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `ui/src/ui/app-render.helpers.node.test.ts` and `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts`.
- Scenario the test should lock in: unnamed dashboard sessions use `sessionStartedAt` for timestamp fallback; explicit labels still win; gateway rows include `sessionStartedAt`.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the behavior is pure display resolution plus one projected row field.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): none.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Unnamed Control UI dashboard sessions now display a timestamp fallback in session pickers/tabs instead of the raw dashboard session key.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
/NEW -> agent:ops:dashboard:<uuid> -> raw key shown when unlabeled

After:
/NEW -> sessionStartedAt projected -> 14:12 / 05-24 14:12 shown when unlabeled
```

- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No
- If any Yes, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

2. Pass it through `resolveSessionDisplayName`.
3. Compare same-day, prior-day, and explicitly labeled rows.

### Expected

- Same-day unnamed dashboard row displays `14:12`.

- Edge cases checked: missing/unnamed row falls back only for dashboard keys; existing label/displayName precedence remains unchanged.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
